correctness.summary: The one-vertex chamber admits an exact simplex-section volume formula from edge-intersection parameters. Angular coordinates reduce the fixed-angle problem to maximizing the product of positive numbers with mean one and fixed variance; Rodin's sharp variance refinement of AM-GM gives the stated profile and equality pattern. The equality tangents are exactly the geodesic directions toward Webb normals, and direct differentiation gives the isotropic Hessian eigenvalue (2n+1)/(n+1).

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: The recent Ambrus--Gargyan work proves the global minimum, Webb gives the global maximum, and Myroshnychenko--Tang--Tatarko--Tkocz treat stability of the maximum. Searches did not locate the exact chamber-wise fixed-angle minimum profile, equality arcs, or isotropic Hessian. The full text of the very recent motivating preprint was not inspected, so an equivalent statement there, in a later revision, or in unindexed parallel work remains the main residual risk.

value.summary: The result gives an exact quantitative stability profile, rather than only a qualitative minimizer classification, throughout a natural normal chamber. It identifies all fixed-angle equality directions and connects the facet minimum continuously to Webb maxima, while also computing the local Hessian exactly.

limitations: The theorem is sharp only inside one-vertex-separating normal chambers and their symmetric copies, not across all normal sign patterns.
It does not reprove the global minimum theorem of Ambrus--Gargyan.
Rodin's fixed-variance AM-GM theorem is a prior ingredient.
The full text of the recent Ambrus--Gargyan preprint was not inspected, leaving residual originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
